header.label: OpenAEC Foundation
header.desc: A tribute to the pioneers of open source. Before it was cool. Before AI existed. When Microsoft still called Linux a cancer. They built the foundations on which we continue to build.

stats.title: Open Source wins
stats.subtitle: The numbers do not lie. Open source is no longer an alternative — it is the standard.

blender.desc: Downloads per week. From niche tool to industry standard. Used by Netflix, NASA, Epic Games.

linux.desc: Of all servers run Linux. 85% of all smartphones (Android), all top-500 supercomputers.

python.desc: Programming language in the world (TIOBE 2026). From scripting to AI, from web to science.

libreoffice.desc: Users worldwide. The free alternative for office applications.

erpnext.desc: Countries where ERPNext is used. Open source ERP that challenges SAP and Oracle.

nextcloud.desc: Users. The open source alternative to Dropbox, Google Drive and OneDrive.

pioneers.title: Pioneers — People
pioneers.subtitle: The people who had the courage to think differently. Who gave their work away so the world would be better for it.

torvalds.desc: The man who built the world's operating system as a hobby project, and later created Git to enable the collaboration of thousands of developers.

vanrossum.desc: The Dutchman who created the most popular programming language in the world. Python is the language of AI, science and the web.

roosendaal.desc: In 2002, crowdfunded €100,000 in 7 weeks to buy Blender free from the bankrupt NaN Technologies. Today Blender is the industry standard for 3D creation.

krijnen.desc: The man behind the open BIM revolution. IfcOpenShell is the backbone of open source BIM tools and makes it possible to read, write and manipulate IFC files.

moult.desc: Pioneer in open source BIM tools. Bonsai makes it possible to create full-fledged BIM models in Blender, entirely open source.

shuttleworth.desc: First African in space. Founded Canonical and made Linux accessible to everyone with Ubuntu.

mehta.desc: Open source ERP that challenges SAP. Frappe Framework and ERPNext prove that enterprise software doesn't have to be expensive and closed.

viegas.desc: "An architect who started coding" — brought open BIM to the web. That Open Company makes it possible to view and edit IFC models directly in the browser.

stallman.role: Founder GNU Project & Free Software Foundation (1983)
stallman.desc: The godfather of free software. Without GNU and the GPL there would be no open source movement as we know it.

ritchie.desc: Without C and UNIX there would be no Linux, no Python, no internet as we know it. The quiet hero whose work made literally everything possible.

hoare.desc: Rust: the language OpenAEC is built on. Safety, speed and reliability without compromises.

hykes.desc: Revolutionized software deployment with containers. Docker made it possible to run software identically anywhere.

karlitschek.desc: Open source alternative to cloud storage. Nextcloud gives users back control over their own data.

projects.title: Open Source Projects
projects.subtitle: The tools and frameworks on which OpenAEC is built. Each project represents years of unpaid work by passionate developers.

linux.desc: The operating system that runs the world. From servers to smartphones.

python.desc: The language anyone can learn. From scripting to machine learning.

blender.desc: 3D creation for everyone. Modeling, animation, rendering and more.

ifcopenshell.desc: The backbone of open BIM. Reading, writing and manipulating IFC files.

bonsai.desc: BIM modeling in Blender. Full-fledged BIM authoring, entirely open source.

thatopen.desc: Open BIM on the web. Viewing and editing IFC models in the browser.

erpnext.desc: Open source ERP. Accounting, project management, CRM and more.

nextcloud.desc: File management and collaboration. Your data, your server, your rules.

docker.desc: Containers for deployment. Running software identically everywhere.

rust.desc: Safe systems programming language. Speed without compromising safety.

libreoffice.desc: Free office applications. Documents, spreadsheets and presentations for everyone.

ubuntu.desc: Linux for everyone. The operating system that brought Linux to the desktop.

git.desc: Version control for the world. Collaborating on code at a global scale.

threejs.desc: 3D graphics on the web. The foundation for interactive 3D experiences in the browser.

pdfjs.desc: PDF rendering in the browser. Open source alternative to proprietary PDF viewers.

tauri.desc: Lightweight desktop apps. Web tech with native performance and small bundles.

closing.quote: We stand on the shoulders of giants. Every line of code we write was made possible by the courage of these pioneers. Open source is not a trend — it is the future.
